name: Sarah
bio: Community social worker supporting vulnerable families, navigating $62,000 in student loan debt, the complex maze of Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF), and stepping into non-profit leadership.

stages.stageTitle: The Social Work Salary & PSLF Maze

selectionSnippet.firstTime: Hello... Sarah here. I just finished my Master of Social Work and took a position at a family shelter making $3,100 a month. But between my undergrad and graduate degrees, I have $62,000 in federal student debt. Standard payments would be $700 a month—over a third of my take-home pay! I need help setting up an Income-Driven Repayment plan for Public Service Loan Forgiveness.
selectionSnippet.returningHelped: Sarah here! You helped me set up my IDR student loan payments so I didn't drown years ago. I'm hitting another major milestone and need your guidance.
selectionSnippet.returningSkipped: Hello, Sarah again. I reached out when I was overwhelmed by my student loans. I've been managing case files at the shelter, but I really need an advisor's eye to keep my PSLF strategy on track.

dialogue.greeting: I love my clients at the shelter with everything I have. But when I come home to a tiny apartment and look at a $62k loan balance, it's hard not to cry. I went to school to help people, not to be trapped in debt forever.
dialogue.planApproved: Oh, what a relief. Setting up my certified Income-Driven Repayment cap at $140/mo and automating an emergency fund means I can continue doing community work without fear.
dialogue.planNeedsWork: Wait, our IDR student loan payment wasn't covered! If I miss an on-time payment, my PSLF qualifying payment counter resets or gets delayed.

lifeEvent.title: PSLF Income-Driven Enrollment
lifeEvent.description: Sarah enrolled in the Public Service Loan Forgiveness program, capping payments to an affordable income percentage ($140/mo).

selectionSnippet.firstTime: Sarah here! I'm 29 and getting married next month! My partner earns $75,000 as a private software developer. But under PSLF, if we file taxes jointly, the government will factor in his income and spike my monthly student loan payment from $160 to nearly $650! We need strategic tax and household budgeting.
selectionSnippet.returningHelped: Sarah! Year 5 of my PSLF certification is officially approved! Even bigger news: I'm getting married! But we need your guidance on navigating Married-Filing-Separately vs Jointly so my loan payments don't explode.
selectionSnippet.returningSkipped: Sarah here again. I couldn't connect with you before. I'm now a licensed clinical social worker getting married, and we really need advice on managing dual-income tax brackets and student loan rules.

dialogue.greeting: Merging two lives is romantic; merging two tax returns when one person is on public loan forgiveness is a legal headache! We want to build an equitable household where neither of us feels penalized.
dialogue.planApproved: This solves our biggest anxiety. By filing separately, we keep my PSLF payment at $160/mo for the final 5 years, while funding our joint home downpayment fund together.
dialogue.planNeedsWork: Wait, our joint emergency buffer isn't funded properly. We need an integrated household safety net.

lifeEvent.title: Dual-Income Marriage & Tax Strategy
lifeEvent.description: Sarah married her partner; filing separately preserves her low PSLF repayment rate while pooling household savings.

selectionSnippet.firstTime: Hello! Sarah here. At 35, the most incredible miracle happened: after 120 qualifying payments over 10 years at non-profits, the Department of Education just officially forgiven my remaining $48,000 student loan balance to $0! Suddenly, I have discretionary cash flow and no debt hanging over my head.
selectionSnippet.returningHelped: Sarah! WE DID IT! The official forgiveness letter arrived: 120 qualifying payments verified, $0 remaining balance! You guided me through every recertification. Now that this giant weight is off my chest, I want to deploy that cash into our first home and retirement.
selectionSnippet.returningSkipped: Sarah here. I persevered through the 10-year PSLF finish line and achieved full forgiveness. I'm ready to build real investments and would love your guidance.

dialogue.greeting: Opening that student aid dashboard and seeing a big green checkmark with '$0.00' balance... I fell to the kitchen floor sobbing with relief. Ten years of public service, and now we are finally financially free.
dialogue.planApproved: This is poetry. Taking the exact monthly amount I used to pay toward student loans and redirecting it into our Roth IRA and home equity feels like reclaiming our future.
dialogue.planNeedsWork: Wait, our Roth IRA or savings allocations are falling short. Now is the time to build wealth, not let money slip away to impulse spending.

lifeEvent.title: PSLF 100% Student Debt Forgiveness
lifeEvent.description: Sarah completed 120 certified payments; her remaining $48,000 federal student loan balance was completely forgiven tax-free.

selectionSnippet.firstTime: Hello! Sarah here at 42. I was recently promoted to Executive Director of our regional youth and family services organization. I oversee a $4M annual operating endowment. Personally, my family is debt-free, and I want to optimize our 403(b) match and personal donor-advised philanthropy.
selectionSnippet.returningHelped: Sarah! From a panic-stricken 24-year-old case worker clutching a $62k loan bill to Executive Director of the entire regional network—you've been my trusted advisor every step. Now I want to structure our family's long-term endowment and retirement.
selectionSnippet.returningSkipped: Sarah here. I've risen to Executive Director of our community agency. I'm looking for an advisor to help with executive retirement benefits and long-term family investments.

dialogue.greeting: Looking at the younger case workers we hire today who carry the same loan anxiety I used to have... being able to advocate for them at the state level is my calling. Having personal financial security allows me to lead fearlessly.
dialogue.planApproved: This architecture is inspirational. Executive 403(b) maximized, high-yield reserves automated, and our family giving fund active. Thank you for a lifetime of support.
dialogue.planNeedsWork: Wait, our executive 403(b) match contributions were left incomplete. Capturing our full employer retirement benefit is essential.

lifeEvent.title: Executive Director Appointment
lifeEvent.description: Sarah was appointed Executive Director of the non-profit organization, receiving executive benefits and 6% 403(b) match.
